items.title: Video Friday: Humanoid Robot Takes On Monkey Bars
items.summary: Humanoid robots are studied in tasks like traversing sparse 3D structures by executing agile whole-body motions. Historical use of robots was documented in urban search and rescue operations following the September 11th attacks. A foundation model like UnifoLM-WLA-1.0 achieved state-of-the-art results by coordinating desktop and whole-body manipulation. Compliance is crucial in physical interaction, demonstrated by work on hybrid impedance-admittance control for aerial robots. Achieving agile and generalized legged locomotion requires integrating perception and control, as detailed in a novel reinforcement learning framework.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Video Friday: Humanoid Robot Takes On Monkey Bars". This report details research into the agile whole-body motions required for humanoid robots to traverse sparse three-dimensional structures, demonstrating advanced whole-body manipulation capabilities. Researchers achieved state-of-the-art results using a foundation model like UnifoLM-WLA-1.0 to coordinate both desktop and whole-body manipulation. The work involved exploring the necessity of compliance in physical interaction, highlighted by research on hybrid impedance-admittance control for aerial robots. Achieving agile and generalized legged locomotion required the integration of perception and control through a novel reinforcement learning framework. This progress indicates a significant step toward more complex and physically interactive robotic systems.

items.title: Building and programming autonomous robots at the York Micromaze Hackathon
items.summary: UK RAS STEPS members participated in a three-day Micromaze Robot Hackathon at the University of York. Teams were challenged to design, build, and program autonomous robots to navigate complex mazes. Participants utilized a Raspberry Pi Pico W platform, MicroPython, and various sensors for collision avoidance. The challenge evaluated robot design, code quality, and wireless control capabilities. The event also aimed to foster future robotics education and outreach opportunities.
items.audio_script: From Robohub, "Building and programming autonomous robots at the York Micromaze Hackathon". This report details a three-day event where UK RAS STEPS members designed, built, and programmed autonomous robots to navigate complex mazes. The event successfully evaluated team skills in robot design, code quality, and wireless control capabilities. Participants employed the Raspberry Pi Pico W platform along with MicroPython and various sensors for implementing collision avoidance systems. The challenge focused on the practical application of programming and sensor integration within a defined navigational task. This initiative aimed to advance robotics education and outreach opportunities within the community. The successful demonstration of these skills points toward continued growth in practical robotics programming and sensor application across the technology sector.
